summary: Initial qualification for rerank/embeddings architecture. ParcelIQ currently uses a hybrid approach with a vector DB for recall (Pinecone) and a CPU-based reranker. They want to understand cost/latency tradeoffs across Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC) options, plus fallback/fanout strategies, dimensioning, and a perf smoke test. transcript:
[00:00:00] Sam: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um starting on time here. Quick intros?
[00:00:10] Chris: Chris here, Head of Search at ParcelIQ, we operate global ecom search and personalization.
[00:00:14] Maya: Maya, ML engineer, own the rerank model and embeddings pipeline.
[00:00:17] Omar: Omar, infra lead, network and compliance owner.
[00:00:20] Leila: Leila with Redwood, SE, I own performance & infra questions. Diego on for deep ops.
[00:00:26] Sam: Great, quick agenda: understand current stack, SLOs and constraints, figure out hosting path, and plan a perf smoke test.
[00:00:36] Chris: We currently use Pinecone for vectors, recall produces ~200 candidates, then a CPU-based transformer rerank on k=50, but latency is a hair too high under load. Looking at moving rerank to GPU for quality and latency.
[00:00:49] Maya: Our embeds are 1024-d from a twins model, we tried 1536 for coverage but cost jumps. Typical QPS is 80-120 at peak, tail P95 needs <300ms end-to-end for search latency, rerank budget is 120ms ideally.
[00:01:05] Omar: Also EU data residency requirement; logs must stay in EU region and we need SOC2 evidence + SAML/SSO integration.
[00:01:12] Leila: Thanks. On the hosting question — Redwood can run Hosted API, Dedicated reserved GPU pools, or Private VPC/on-prem. For 80-120 QPS and a 120ms rerank target, we typically recommend Dedicated with autoscale or a hybrid: host recall in Pinecone, run rerank on Redwood Dedicated with KV-cache for prefixes.
[00:01:30] Chris: Can you explain KV cache? Our caches are messy, what does Redwood mean by KV?
[00:01:33] Leila: Yeah, kv as in key-value cache for decoder states — avoids re-computing prefix tokens for chat, for rerank we use prefix caching for document context and partial k-v reuse across requests. That can drop token work by 20-35% depending on overlap.
[00:01:45] Maya: Hm okay. How does that interact with sharded vector DB fanout? If we recall from 4 shards, we might get duplicated contexts.
[00:01:52] Diego: We usually de-dup at the recall layer; Redwood's routing can also fold identical contexts into the same rerank call or parallelize within the GPU pool. The goal is to reduce duplicate tokenization + reduce network hop count.
[00:02:04] Maya: What about quantization — we care about 8-bit/4-bit for latency/cost, but worried about ranking quality regression.
[00:02:10] Leila: Right. We support quantized inference paths and have quality profiles per model/quantization level. For rerank, we recommend running a 16-bit or 8-bit fp16 path for initial eval; 4-bit aggressive quant can save more but must be validated on your eval set. We can run a quality sweep during the perf test.
[00:02:25] Chris: Does Redwood integrate directly with Pinecone or will we proxy calls through our VPC?
[00:02:29] Sam: Two options — let Redwood talk to Pinecone over the internet from Hosted, or in Dedicated/Private we can colocate in your VPC so traffic stays internal. For EU residency and hardened audit, Private (VPC) or Dedicated inside an EU region is typical.
[00:02:42] Omar: Important — we need KMS integration for keys and audit logs shipped to our SIEM.
[00:02:46] Leila: We support KMS/HSM integrations and streaming audit logs; we'll attach the security doc.
[00:02:50] Maya: Back to throughput — you mentioned batching, how does Redwood decide batch size versus tail latency? We can't let P95 blow past 300ms.
[00:02:58] Diego: We have an adaptive batching system that takes request arrival patterns into account. For low latency SLOs we prioritize small batches and continuous batching; for high throughput windows we increase batch size. You can set a SLO policy per route that biases towards latency or cost.
[00:03:12] Chris: If we run rerank on Redwood Hosted API to start, what's the unit cost roughly?
[00:03:17] Sam: We'll send the hosted vs dedicated spreadsheet, but ballpark hosted for rerank (GPU-backed gen) is higher per call than dedicated reserved capacity. Hosted is great for quick trials; Dedicated reduces unit cost at scale.
[00:03:28] Maya: For the perf smoke test, we want to replay 1k QPS burst traces, real query set, and measure end-to-end: recall, network, rerank. Can Redwood run that in a sandbox?
[00:03:36] Leila: Yes, we can stand up a Dedicated pool in test mode for a 2-hour blast — many customers do that. We'll capture per-token breakdown, GPU utilization, and tail latency.
[00:03:44] Omar: About sharding vector DB — if we put Pinecone cross-region, cost and tail latency blow up. Any recommendations?
[00:03:50] Diego: We usually co-locate the vector DB in the same region as rerank GPUs or run an edge cache for embeddings. Another pattern is embedding pre-sharding and local fanout only within region. We'll discuss alignment options in the post-call materials.
[00:04:02] Chris: Competitor question — we've chatted with Pinecone about reducing recall to top 100 and then rerank. Any reason to pick Redwood over a self-hosted inference stack?
[00:04:10] Sam: Redwood provides unified serving + routing + rollout + observability designed for production economics. If you self-host, you need the batching, cache, fallback policies, and observability that we've built — otherwise you risk higher op cost.
[00:04:22] Maya: How do we validate ranking quality if we change model size or quantization? We need eval hooks.
[00:04:27] Leila: Redwood Optimize has quality monitoring tied to prompt sets and evals; we can run regression checks during canary deploys and score against your golden set. We'll include the Optimize overview.
[00:04:37] Omar: On SSO — SAML enterprise SSO is required, plus fine-grained role-based access.
[00:04:41] Leila: We support SAML, OIDC, and RBAC. We'll send the admin docs.
[00:04:46] Chris: Let's talk numbers — if we aim for 80 QPS steady and 150 QPS burst, with rerank top-50 per query, what GPUs do you recommend?
[00:04:54] Diego: Initial recommendation: 2x A10/A100-equivalent nodes with autoscale to add 1 more on bursts; with continuous batching and 8-bit quant path you should hit cost targets while keeping P95 under 300ms. For sustained 150 QPS at top-50 rerank you'd benefit from Dedicated pools sized to match your peak. We'll provide a sizing calc in the spreadsheet.
[00:05:10] Maya: Any note on embedding dimensions — we are considering moving from 1024 to 768 to reduce fanout work, but worried about recall loss.
[00:05:16] Leila: That's a classical tradeoff. We can run a dimension-sweep in the eval with your dataset: 768 vs 1024 vs 1536 and measure recall+rerank delta. Often you can compress with minimal recall loss if you retrain or use a smaller scorer.
[00:05:28] Chris: Talk to me about fallback strategies if Dedicated goes down or a zone loses capacity.
[00:05:33] Sam: Redwood supports automated fallback policies — route to a lower-capacity model variant or fall back to hosted in another region. For strict SLAs you can configure cross-region fallbacks and keep a standby small pool.
[00:05:44] Omar: We'll need to see SLOs and any SLA credits in writing.
[00:05:47] Sam: We'll include SLA summary in the follow-up.
[00:05:50] Maya: Ok, next practicals — perf test week of May 26 works. We'll provide the 1k query sample and an eval set.
[00:05:57] Leila: Great. Action recap?
[00:06:00] Sam: Sam to send cost vs hosting spreadsheet, Leila to send security pack + SOC2, Diego to propose sizing calc, Maya to share sample traces. We'll schedule the perf smoke test and get agreement signed for the eval.
[00:06:11] Chris: Sounds good, thanks all.
[00:06:14] Omar: Thanks.
[00:06:16] Leila: Thanks everyone, will follow up.
[00:06:20] [call ends early notes truncated]
